narrative.overview:
Harness reads like the live timing graphics of a race broadcast laid over a developer's desk. A graphite tower runs down the left edge in both light and dark mode, listing every session the way a timing tower lists cars: a square status flag, a short name, and a condensed lap time ticking on the right. The work area beside it is cool and quiet: white in light mode, graphite in dark. Progress and history are drawn as rows of timed sectors, never as smooth bars. Every number is set in Barlow Semi Condensed tabular figures, so times, costs and percentages line up and can be read from across the room.

The system is dense and calm on purpose. Most controls are 28px high, most type is 12 or 13px, and structure comes from hairlines and small tonal steps rather than shadows. Colour is scarce and always means something. There are four timing colours, each with one job: green means running or done, yellow means waiting for you, red means failed, and violet marks the best result and the one primary action. Everything else is ink, slate and graphite. One thing moves: a highlight sweeping across the live sector, like a sector being timed.

The world refuses the category default: a grey macOS sidebar, white panes, one brand-orange accent and smooth progress bars. It should read as clearly at 3 a.m. on a hackathon weekend as on a Tuesday afternoon.
keyCharacteristics: A graphite rail (the timing tower) in both modes; anything inside it, menus included, switches to dark tokens.
Mini-sector strips wherever progress or history shows: run steps, HackForge phases, tool calls, milestones, meters.
Condensed tabular figures for every readout; the same face at heading size.
Four timing colours with one job each, each a fill paired with a text-safe ink.
Crisp corners from 1px to a 10px ceiling, square status flags and 28px controls.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines; shadows only on things that float.
One primary button per screen or card; everything else sits behind ▾, ⋯, the / menu or ⌘K.

rules.name: The Four Flags Rule
rules.body: Green is running or done, yellow is waiting for you, red is failed, violet is best. A state never borrows another state's colour, and grey means ready or still to come. If a new state does not fit one of the four, it is ink.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Solid violet does exactly two jobs: the one primary action and the best result. Its tint and ink mark only what you have chosen or focused. Violet never signals that something is running, waiting or merely present: status dots, spinners, count badges and any progress bar that is not a best result are never violet.

rules.name: The Fill-and-Ink Rule
rules.body: Dots, sectors and bars use the base colour; text uses its `-ink` partner, which holds at least 5.4:1 on the surface in both modes. Never set text in a fill colour.

rules.name: The Ink-for-Amounts Rule
rules.body: Plain amounts (context used, plan usage) fill in ink at 70%, not green. They turn yellow and then red near their limits: context past 65% and 85%, the 5-hour plan window past 70% and 90% (or when the plan warns or rejects). Usage left (a teammate's headroom) fills the same ink and turns yellow at 30% left and red at 10% left.

rules.name: The Graphite Rail Rule
rules.body: The rail is graphite in both modes and re-scopes every token inside it to its dark values, so menus opened from the rail are dark too. The same graphite material is reused as the command well that shows a running shell command inside an agent card. Any other always-dark surface takes the same re-scope, so its text uses the dark-mode `-ink` values, never raw palette colours.

rules.name: The Condensed Readout Rule
rules.body: Every time, cost, percentage, token count and score is set in Barlow Semi Condensed with tabular figures. A number in the platform sans is a bug.

rules.name: The Three-Size Rule
rules.body: The interface runs on 13, 12 and 11px. 14px appears only where you type at length (the Home prompt, the ⌘K input) and in the Home lede. The display face takes over at heading size (18px and up) and nowhere smaller, except in labels and readouts.

rules.name: The Label, Not Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Uppercase labels name a column, a group or a tile. They never sit above a heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat on hairlines. A shadow means the thing floats (pop), is where you start (prompt lift) or responds to the pointer (hover lift). Cards, panels and tiles never carry a resting shadow.

rules.name: The Ten-Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No corner exceeds 10px, and most are 4–6px. Pills belong only to switches and play buttons.

rules.name: The Square Flag Rule
rules.body: Status markers are squares: 8px at 2px radius, or 6px at 1px inline. A round status dot breaks the timing-board language.

rules.name: The One Button Rule
rules.body: Each screen or card has exactly one primary (violet) button. Alternatives go behind its ▾; everything else goes behind ⋯, the / menu or ⌘K.

rules.name: The One Sweep Rule
rules.body: The highlight crossing the live sector (1.6s, `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, repeating) is the only ambient animation, and only the leading sector of a live meter carries it; the sectors behind it are plain done. No opacity pulses, breathing dots or shimmer. The only other motions are functional: the stepped caret while text streams, a spinner standing in for an icon while something runs (slate, info blue for an in-progress task, or the busy button's own label colour; never violet), and 150ms colour and shadow transitions on hover. The sweep, the caret and every spinner stop under reduced motion.

dos: Do draw every progress, history or usage reading as mini-sectors with 2px gaps and 1px corners.
Do set every readout (time, cost, percentage, count, score) in Barlow Semi Condensed with tabular figures.
Do keep the rail graphite (#15161d light, #0e0f14 dark) in both modes and let anything that opens inside it inherit the dark tokens.
Do give each screen or card exactly one violet primary button and put its alternatives behind an attached ▾.
Do mark status with 8px squares at 2px radius: green running, yellow waiting for you, red failed, idle grey for ready.
Do fill plain amounts in ink at 70% and switch them to yellow, then red, as they near their limits.
Do pair every state fill with its `-ink` partner for text, and set text on yellow in rail graphite.
Do keep UI text at 13/12/11px and use the condensed display face for headings at 18px and up.
Do separate surfaces with 1px hairlines and tonal steps; reserve shadows for floating layers, the prompt box and agent-card hover.
Do assign categorical colours in series order, and tint tool kinds at 10% fill and 28% border with the colour on the icon only.
donts: Don't use a grey macOS sidebar, white panes with a single brand-orange accent, or smooth continuous progress bars; that is the category default Harness refuses.
Don't use violet to say something is running, waiting or new: no violet status dots, spinners, count badges or progress bars except for a best result.
Don't animate anything but the live sector's sweep: no opacity pulses, breathing dots or shimmer skeletons.
Don't use round status dots or pill-shaped badges; status is square and badges have 3px corners.
Don't set a number in the platform sans, and don't set body copy in the condensed face.
Don't put an uppercase label above a heading as an eyebrow; labels name columns, groups and tiles.
Don't set text in a fill colour (yellow, green or idle grey) or white text on green or yellow fills.
Don't fill a destructive action solid red; outline it, and put it behind ⋯ with a confirm.
Don't cycle categorical colours or reassign a tool kind's colour.
